unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We denote $\rho_*:=P_*(A=0)\in(0,1)$, the true proportion of data from the target population.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Observed-target proportion for Theorem 2 and dagger specializations. It is not a positivity assumption on an unobserved target in the general Section 3 setup.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We suppose that $\operatorname{var}_{P_*}(\ell(X,Y)\mid A=0)<\infty$, a very mild condition, throughout this paper.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Footnote 2, standing finite target-loss variance. Its X,Y and A=0 wording must be preserved alongside the later generalized Z,Q setting.
Footnote 3 supplies a stated zero-denominator convention; do not report every zero fold count as completely unspecified. It does not define a nonzero numerator divided by zero.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For any non-negative integers $M$ and $N$, we use $[M:N]$ to denote the index set $\{M,M+1,\ldots,N\}$ if $M\leq N$ and the empty index set otherwise; we use $[M]$ as a shorthand for $[1:M]$. For any finite set $S$, we use $|S|$ to denote its cardinality.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Finite fold and component ranges, including the empty sums arising when K=1.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
For a distribution $P$, we use $P_\sharp$ and $P_{\sharp\mid
atural}$ to denote the marginal distribution of the random variable $\sharp$ and the conditional distribution of $\sharp\mid
atural$, respectively, under $P$; we use $P_{*,\sharp}$ and $P_{*,\sharp\mid
atural}$ to denote these distributions under $P_*$. We use $P^n$ to denote the empirical distribution of a sample of size $n$ from $P$. When splitting the sample into $V>0$ folds, we use $P^{n,v}$ and $P_\sharp^{n,v}$ to denote empirical distributions in fold $v\in[V]$. All functions considered will be measurable with respect to appropriate sigma-algebras, which will be kept implicit. For any function $f$, any distribution $P$, we sometimes use $Pf$ to denote $\int f\,dP$. For any $p\in[1,\infty]$, we use $\|f\|_{L^p(P)}$ to denote the $L^p(P)$ norm of $f$, namely $(\int f(x)^pP(dx))^{1/p}$. We also use $L^p(P)$ to denote the space of all functions with a finite $L^p(P)$ norm, and use $L_0^p(P)$ to denote $\{f\in L^p(P):\int f\,dP=0\}$. All asymptotic results are with respect to the sample size $n$ tending to infinity.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original ambient notation. The printed Lp formula lacks absolute values and an infinity-endpoint definition. L2 and L2_0 are used by the two theorem statements; do not silently rewrite the general notation.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: When working under this stronger condition, we use $\mathcal S_k$ to denote $\mathcal S'_k\setminus\{0\}$ for short.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Source-only sets exclude the observed target. The preceding stronger condition is DS.0-dagger; S_k can be empty, whereas S-prime_k is nonempty in DS.0.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: According to the well-known review by Moreno-Torres et al. [2012], the following four dataset shift conditions are among the most widely considered when one source population is available, so that $\mathcal A=\{0,1\}$. These conditions are all special cases of Condition $\mathrm{DS.0}^\dagger$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Binary one-source context for DS.1 and Section 4. DS.2–DS.4 are not hypotheses of Theorem 2.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: If $\theta^{k-1}(\bar z_{k-1})=\infty$, we set $1/(1+\theta^{k-1}(\bar z_{k-1}))$ to be zero. When $\theta^{k-1}$ equals the truth $\theta_*^{k-1}$, this can happen for $\bar z_{k-1}$ outside the support of $\bar Z_{k-1}\mid A=0$ but inside the support of $\bar Z_{k-1}\mid A\in\mathcal S_k$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Footnote 4 fixes the inverse-odds convention at infinity; preserve it for (7), (9), (13) and the dagger algorithm.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We take as given a flexible regression method $\mathcal K$ estimating conditional means and a flexible classifier $\mathcal C$ estimating conditional odds—both taking outcome, covariates, and an index set for data points being used as inputs in order. For example, $\mathcal K$ and $\mathcal C$ may be random forests, neural networks, gradient boosting, or an ensemble learner. We also take as given a flexible density ratio estimator $\mathcal W$, taking an index set for data points being used as input, which may be transformed from a classifier $\mathcal C$ by Bayes’ Theorem or based on kernel density estimators.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Given fitting procedures; no particular learner or sufficient smoothness condition is an extra theorem premise. The general algorithm body remains excluded.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Splitting the sample into a fixed number $V$ of folds $I_v$ ($v\in[V]$) leads to the estimating equation $\sum_{i\in I_v}D_{\mathrm{SC}}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}_v,r)(O_i)=0$ averaging over data in each every fold $v$, with preliminary estimators $(\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}_v)$ using data outside of the fold. The solution is given in (11).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Fixed V asymptotic convention. The source says every preliminary estimate uses out-of-fold data here, but Algorithm 1-dagger line 4 uses in-fold pi. Preserve the discrepancy and the actual algorithm.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: It is viable to replace the in-fold estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}_v$ of $\boldsymbol\pi_*$ with an out-of-fold estimator in Algorithms 1 and $1^\dagger$. These two approaches have the same theoretical properties that we will show next, and similar empirical performance.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark 2 records an allowed alternative in the general/dagger discussion. This does not erase the different qualification about inconsistent conditional-risk estimation in Section 4 Remark 6.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In the following analyses without assuming Condition DS.0, we assume that nuisance estimators $\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v$ can be evaluated at any point in the space $\mathcal Z$ containing the observation, even if that point is outside the support under $P_*$. For illustration, we assume that, for each $k\in[2:K]$, $\|\widehat\ell_v^k-\ell_\infty^k\|_{L^2(\nu_k)}\xrightarrow{p}0$ for some function $\ell_\infty^k$, where $\nu_k$ denotes the distribution of $\bar Z_k\mid A\in\mathcal S'_k$ under $P^0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Off-support evaluability is a stated convention. The limiting regressions are illustrative only, as Remark 3 makes explicit. The source writes the otherwise unexplained P^0; do not replace it with P_*.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In all expectations involving nuisance estimators such as $(\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_v,\widehat{\boldsymbol\pi}_v)$, these estimators are treated as fixed and the expectation integrates over the randomness in a data point $O=(Z,A)$. For example, $\mathbb E_{P_*}[\widehat\ell_v^1(Z_1)\mid A=0]=\int\widehat\ell_v^1\,d\mu$ where $\mu$ is the distribution of $Z_1\mid A=0$ under $P_*$, and this expectation is itself random due to the randomness in $\widehat\ell_v^1$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Footnote 5: fitted nuisance functions remain random, but are frozen for integration over a fresh observation. This governs h, B, Delta and the remainder in Theorem 2.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Further, given any scalar $r$, with $\theta^0:=\sum_{a\in\mathcal S_1}\pi^a/\pi^0$, define
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Generic theta^0 convention preceding (8), also used in (7) and (9). It does not make D_GSC a prerequisite of D_SC.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Conditions ST.1 and ST.2 can hold even if the limit $\ell_\infty^k$ of the nuisance function estimator $\widehat\ell_v^k$ does not exist. This case could happen if the support of $\bar Z_k\mid A\in\mathcal S_k$ is larger than $\mathcal Z_k$. Our results allow for such cases; we introduced the limit $\ell_\infty^k$ to illustrate Conditions ST.1 and ST.2.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark 3 expressly limits the role of the illustrative nuisance limits; they are not extra hypotheses of Theorem 1.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Nevertheless, without Condition DS.0, our results in Section 3.2 remain valid as long as Condition ST.1 or ST.2 holds for one version of the collection of true conditional mean loss functions $\boldsymbol\ell_*$. For example, part 2 of Condition ST.1 would require the consistency of $\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v$ for some version of $\boldsymbol\ell_*$, and $D_{\mathrm{SC}}(\boldsymbol\ell_*,\boldsymbol\theta_*,\boldsymbol\pi_*,r_*)$ in (22) would depend on the particular adopted version of $\boldsymbol\ell_*$. The appropriate choice of $\boldsymbol\ell_*$ often depends on the asymptotic behavior of the nuisance estimator $\widehat{\boldsymbol\ell}_v$, which might heavily depend on the particular choice of the regression technique used in the sequential regression (Line 6, Alg. $1^\dagger$).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Section 3.4 qualification: under failed DS.0, rate conditions and the influence function can depend on the adopted conditional-mean version. No unique global version is imposed.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: It is possible to replace the in-fold estimator $\widehat\rho^v$ of $\rho_*$ with an out-of-fold estimator in Alg. 1. Unlike Alg. $1^\dagger$, this would lead to a different influence function when the nuisance function $\mathcal E_*$ is estimated inconsistently in Theorem 2. In this case, the influence function of $\widehat r_{\mathrm{Xcon}}$ from Theorem 2 cannot be used to construct asymptotically valid confidence intervals if $\mathcal E_*$ is estimated inconsistently.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark 6 qualifies the alternative rho estimate in the concept-shift algorithm and supports retaining the inconsistent fold superscripts in the printed Theorem 2 remainder.

source_issues.description: All statements and passages refer to the registered arXiv v4, stamped 8 Jun 2024, not an assumed published-version transcription.

The general Algorithm 1 is explicitly placed in the supplement. Only the main-text reference and Theorem 1 input/output references are preserved. Its construction and omitted local dependencies remain unresolved.
General supplement Algorithm 1, main-text Algorithm 1-dagger on page 15, and Section 4 Algorithm 1 on page 26 are distinct source references. The two latter bodies are retained in full.

Section 2 assumes A contains 0 and fully observed target data. Section 3 expressly allows an unobserved target Q. Theorem 1 still writes conditional expectations given A=0 in Delta; that notation requires clarification in the general unobserved-target case.
The prefix setup names the support of history given A=0 even though Q may be unobserved. DS.0 subsequently says support under Q. Preserve both source formulations.

Theorem 1 discusses failure of DS.0 yet uses lambda_* defined for dominated target/source history laws. The main-text failure discussion emphasizes conditional mismatch and extensions; no unrestricted density-ratio construction under failure of domination is supplied.

DS.0 makes S-prime_k a known nonempty subset but does not separately write positive source probability for every such conditioning event. Conditional laws and denominators need their usual existence conventions.

Footnote 2 states finite conditional variance of ell(X,Y) given A=0 throughout, while the generalized setup permits arbitrary Z and unobserved Q. Do not silently change that standing source statement.

Fixed V is stated in Section 3.2. Approximately equal fold sizes are specified by Algorithm 1-dagger; the specialized Algorithm 1 states random folds without repeating approximate equality. Empty-fold handling and minimum training class sizes are not fully specified.

Page 14 says all preliminary nuisance estimators are out-of-fold. Algorithm 1-dagger explicitly estimates pi in-fold. Remark 2 permits an out-of-fold alternative; preserve the actual recipe and both qualifications.
The last denominator in expansion (19) uses pi_v^a without a hat. Its meaning is not separately defined; it is preserved rather than silently replaced by pi-hat_v^a.
The threshold on t contains a*b+a+b+n^-1, whereas the normal-tail bound (20) contains a*b+n^-1/2*(a+b)+n^-1. Both are preserved as printed.

The finite-sample branch quantifies over all n,k,v and refers to the bound on lambda-hat. It does not separately spell out whether one deterministic envelope is uniform in all indices and realizations; the constants are stated to depend only on epsilon, P_* and that bound.
Theorem 1 divides by sigma_*,GSC in (20), without explicitly assuming it is positive. The source 0/0=0 convention does not specify nonzero/0.
ST.1 and ST.2 control r-hat minus Delta. DS.0 is added only in the final clause to make Delta=0. Drift correction must not be discarded or DS.0 added to every branch.

Section 3.4 says conditional means can be nonunique even on target supports when DS.0 fails; ST conditions and the influence function may depend on the selected version. No unique canonical regression is substituted.
Remark 3 allows ST.1/ST.2 without existence of every nuisance limit. The illustrative L2(nu_k) convergence and limiting oracle regressions are not added as theorem assumptions.
The illustration defining nu_k on page 14 uses P^0 without a definition there. That symbol is preserved as an unresolved source convention.
The stated general Lp norm lacks absolute values and the infinity-endpoint convention, although p ranges through infinity. The actual theorem uses L2. Preserve the printed general definition.

Asymptotic linearity and efficient influence function are described in the main text, but regularity and full model/tangent-space definitions are not provided. Supplementary efficiency exposition remains excluded.

The paragraph identifying D_GSC and D_SC as efficient influence functions requires DS.0 plus two-sided ratio bounds or DS.0-dagger plus bounded odds. These conditions qualify that source identification; they must not be silently inserted into all of Theorem 1.
DS.1 is X independent of A under A={0,1}. Neither a multi-source interpretation of 1-a nor Y|X invariance is substituted for it.

Theorem 2 remainder uses rho-hat^v in its first term but rho-hat^{-v} inside D_Xcon. Algorithm 1 estimates rho in-fold. Remark 6 says out-of-fold rho changes the influence function when conditional risk is inconsistently estimated; preserve the apparent inconsistency.
Theorem 2 assumes one common L2 limit across folds, which need not equal E_*. The extra leading influence-function term is retained. Only the final branch sets E_infinity=E_*.
Theorem 1 footnote 6 is retained as source_footnotes in the inventory and must survive the full census handoff unchanged. It is not inserted into statement_original.

Ordinary conditional expectation, RN derivatives, stochastic orders, standard normal probability, finite sums and convergence remain ambient.

1.local_objects: Theorem 1 explicitly consumes estimated and true nuisance functions, both pseudo-loss parameterizations through its algorithm references, h, B, sigma_GSC, ST.1/ST.2 and the final additional DS.0 clause. General r_*=E_Q ell and the dagger observed-target specialization must remain distinguishable.
1.ambient_or_bound: Delta_v and Delta, confidence sequences a,b,c,d, epsilon,t, constants C1/C2, and Phi are bound or defined inline. The nuisance integration convention freezes fitted functions. pi_v^a in (19), A=0 for an unobserved target, and missing general algorithm details remain unresolved.
1.branch_scope: Retain finite-sample expansion and confidence guarantee, two algorithm-specific efficiency expansions, weaker consistency, and final drift-zero conclusion as branches of one theorem.
